name: The compass
tagline: Draws a map over the car showing where a cut would make it faster.
what: Looks at one car and draws a map over its whole surface: where pushing the surface in or out would make the race time faster or slower.
One special simulation gives the whole map for about the cost of one normal run.
The cutter carves along this map, so the map must be proven against real measurements before anyone trusts it.
If the fast map cannot be made right, a slower map built from direct measurements is the backup.

items.name: Map placed on the car surface

now: Compass test: 45 carved cars timing on 2 cores across main, mxnviir, instagramshashank8-bot, Jdiejei, anasssssssss1 and the blackwing accounts. Stuck blackwingstem-wq cars move a few at a time to idle accounts (force-cancel first, then a fresh one-car run). Cars 1-2 (4 cores) are re-running failed jobs. No car judged yet. Slow pace while Q8 is open.

log.text: Wing test, first result: the map says the opposite of the measured change on all twenty bumps, and the flow run was stopping long before it had settled. Both look like real causes of the old bad results.
Board created. Waiting for the go to start this phase.
Repository cleaned: the old carving loop is removed. The compass will be built fresh and proven. All tests pass.
Started. Read the code: found a likely mix-up about which way the surface points, to be checked first on a simple wing.

Changed the shared map tool (in the stopwatch folder) for Part 2 to know: the map now reads the surface direction the right way round, and its flow run no longer stops early. Proven on the wing test: the map now has the right direction on all twenty bumps.
Nose test on eighteen real cars: the map now says growing the nose adds drag on every one. Still open: the car flow does not fully settle, and the map misses about one twelfth of the car surface.
Map to race time: built and checked against the race model, including where the weight sits now that the race time accounts for it. All unit tests pass.
Wing test: the fast map fails on every setting tried, the backup measured map passes. The car test waits for quieter car runs.

Backup measured map on the wing: matched shapes outside its own building blocks too, except very narrow bumps below its resolution. The fast map size gap is a missing term in its simple formula, not a units error.
Backup measured map also passed on a four times finer wing mesh and with twice as many building blocks; only tiny narrow bumps are below its resolution.
One-cut rehearsal on the wing: small steps along the backup map lowered drag clearly; steps four times larger made it worse, so cuts must stay small.

Hardened wing result: the backup measured map was tested on twenty shapes it was never built from (narrow, wide and mixed bumps). It followed the true changes closely and had the direction right on eighteen of twenty, on both the normal and the four times finer mesh. The two misses are very narrow bumps, finer than the map can see.
Restarted on the main account only, a few machines at a time. Now checking whether the fast map on a car stays the same when the unsteady flow is stopped at different moments.

Map steadiness on two cars: the fast map came out almost the same at three different moments of the swinging flow, with the direction agreeing on about nineteen of every twenty points and on every one of the strongest points. The map now reaches all but about two in a hundred points of the real car surface; the rest are on the flat closing face at the middle. One open point stays: the fast map still says growing the whole car evenly lowers drag, which is physically wrong, so it remains a side study and the measured map stays first.

Car pilot ready: a small trial on one car ran end to end on the main account (about 1 machine-hour). One finding for Part 2: pulling the nose tip in by a millimetre made the reshaped mesh fail its check, so that car was meshed fresh; the pilot now leaves such pairs out instead of mixing mesh types.

Back at full speed. Built the car test of the backup measured map: the map comes from small bumps on one carved car, and is then checked against random shapes cut by Part 1's cutter that it was never built from, with the same pass marks as the compass test. Proof write-up started.

Compass test on two carved cars is running on the teammate accounts. Part 5 carving loop started: its keep rule passes the noise test, and a wrong compass never makes a car slower; reaching the best car often enough is still being worked on.

Carving loop: tried a smarter step that follows bends, a faster shrink, more rounds and a longer final check. None lifted the curved-valley shape to the mark, and two made a simple shape slightly worse, so all four were undone. Now logging each round of the failing runs to find the one real cause.

Decision: the fast map is dropped because it failed the known-answer test on every setting. The measured map, built from direct timings, is now the compass. 45 carved cars are timing for the compass test; new runs go out slowly after two accounts were suspended.

agent_note: Measured map is the compass (fast map dropped). Loop keeps up to 256 re-times per step. Compass test cars are timing; the result decides whether the compass needs averaging before any real loop run.

tasks.title: Known-answer test
tasks.note: Fast map fails on every setting tried, including the maker's own full setup; the measured map passes. Decided 2026-11-13: fast map dropped, the measured map is the compass.

tasks.title: Compass test on the car
tasks.note: Running on 45 carved cars (2 cores), a few moved at a time between accounts: the measured map is built from small bumps, then checked against 40 random cuts per car. No car judged yet. Pass: direction right on 8 of 10 cuts that clearly change the time, and a close match overall.

tasks.title: Fixes, tried in order
tasks.note: Stopped: no setting of the fast map passed the known-answer test, so it is no longer tuned.

tasks.title: Measured map (now the compass)
tasks.note: Passed on the simple wing: matched every test shape it had not seen. Now the compass for every car: 54 timing jobs per car (start car, 60 bumps, 40 cuts), run on Part 3's accounts at the slow pace.
